summary: Keyword co-occurrence in bundled Solana web3.js library — semantic verification needed
details: Pattern matches fired on the package's bundled CommonJS and ESM outputs (lib/index.cjs.js and lib/index.esm.js) for co-occurrence of require('child_process'), fetch/POST, and the strings 'curl' and 'ping' within a large minified/bundled main. This is the published @solana-labs/web3.js client SDK whose documented purpose is HTTP/WS RPC to Solana nodes (fetch calls to caller-configured RPC endpoints) and which historically has bundled or referenced node-fetch/whatwg-fetch shims that include child_process and curl/ping tokens as part of platform-detection or test scaffolding. No hardcoded attacker C2 endpoint, credential path read, env-var scrape, lifecycle script, or install-time exec was identified in the available evidence; the references to 'curl' and 'ping' appear as string tokens rather than as traced execution paths. Routing to human review to semantically verify whether the flagged spans are user-facing API surface (RPC client with caller-configured URL) or an actual install/import-time exfil path before publishing a verdict.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
